note: He matches four of the five stated criteria and fails hard on the fifth, which makes him the cleanest illustration in this batch of what the ICP is actually screening for. A construction coordinator and field engineer who previously worked on a NASA launch pad and now holds what he calls a high-profile role is a credible read of successful. Neglected_health fits precisely as the quote describes it - active his whole life, then posted to a desk job and 'here lately at work, I've just been sitting at a desk, and I can feel it' - a neglected area rather than a crisis. He is 180 lb aiming for 170-175, does 20-30 pushups, and wants to tighten up and rebuild leg strength, so he is good-to-great rather than rescue and nowhere near the deconditioned exclusion. Income fails outright and terminally: his stated ceiling is three figures and he ended the call over a four-figure range. Judged on the criteria as written and not on the outcome - though in this case the outcome and the criterion are the same fact. The interesting question the assessment raises is whether income is the right screen or whether, as with other cases in this corpus, it is filtering out a well-qualified buyer that a cheaper tier could have carried.
